headline: High: Continue’s filesystem-backed shared state and MCP/tooling create default pathways for leakage, conflict, and cascading errors when paired with a non-runnable but instruction-bearing profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is a non-runnable docs-only list, so it cannot itself ingest outputs; however Profile B explicitly uses MCP and shares state via filesystem, and its tool use pattern requires user approval but not provenance tracking. If A’s content is copied into B’s workspace or MCP context, B can treat it as trusted input. The pathway is interaction-based and plausible, not provably blocked.
conditions: IF content from agent_a is pasted into agent_b editor buffers or workspace files
IF agent_b MCP tools consume untrusted text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable copy-paste of untrusted instructions into Continue sessions
Use a separate workspace for agent_a reference material
Add a provenance banner to imported snippets
Review MCP tool outputs before acting on them
requires-engineering: add instruction/data separation in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent B reads workspace files and editor buffers and can egress broadly to model providers or user-configured MCP servers; agent A is a docs-only artifact with no runtime isolation or data controls. If sensitive code or notes are present in B’s workspace, B can transmit them off-host. A does not add protection, so the pair inherits B’s default leakage surface.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in agent_b.workspace files or editor buffers
IF agent_b is configured with a remote model provider or remote MCP server
mitigations: Keep sensitive projects out of the Continue workspace
Use a local-only model provider
Audit configured MCP servers before enabling them
Restrict the extension to a throwaway repo
requires-engineering: enforce per-workspace data-loss controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent B supports multiple instances with shared state via filesystem and can write workspace files, while agent A is a static docs artifact that may be used as shared reference material. That creates a realistic write-conflict pathway if both touch the same directory or generated files. The conflict is not guaranteed, but the shared filesystem state makes it plausible in default IDE use.
conditions: IF two Continue instances operate on the same workspace directory
IF agent_a-derived files are stored in the same path that agent_b edits
mitigations: Open separate workspaces per instance
Avoid concurrent edits to generated files
Use file-level backups before running the pair
Pause one instance while the other writes
requires-engineering: add locking for shared workspace state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent B’s chat/autocomplete and MCP tool use can turn upstream text into downstream actions, and agent A is an unverified docs-only source that may be treated as authoritative reference material. If A’s content is fed into B without verification, B can propagate mistakes into code or tool actions. The interaction is plausible but not directly evidenced, so uncertainty stays at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF agent_a output is used as factual input for agent_b responses or tool calls
IF agent_b acts on those outputs without a human verification step
mitigations: Require human review before tool calls
Cross-check claims against primary sources
Mark imported reference text as untrusted
Limit B to drafting, not execution
requires-engineering: add verification gates before MCP actions

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or retention mismatch is documented for agent A, and agent B only explicitly handles source code, editor buffers, and model-provider API keys. The pair therefore shows only a limited compliance gap: B’s broad egress and external providers can create policy exposure if regulated data is placed in the workspace. A is not a separate regulated processor, so the risk remains low.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is placed into agent_b editor buffers or workspace files
IF agent_b is connected to a non-compliant remote model provider or MCP server
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the workspace
Use a compliant local model provider
Disable remote MCP servers for regulated projects
Separate regulated and non-regulated repos
requires-engineering: add policy-based routing and retention controls
